sources: records.data.executionReadiness in the committed SRD pack
2026-07-06 execution-boundary, engine-coverage, rule-classification, and magic-item inventories
current @eshyra/core implementation and current open/closed beads
source clauses identified by those findings but absent from current projection

rows.requirement: Evaluate condition and eligibility relations as a deterministic predicate before an effect or option is selected
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: select records whose data.executionReadiness clauses have an engine hook where ('engine:' + hook.engine) == 'engine:F1' and hook.hook contains condition or eligibility, then emit record.key; no count is stored.
rows.codeEvidence: Structured condition relations and eligibility checks exist in the core state and rules paths, but every source clause still needs a provider-neutral execution owner.
rows.notes: Primitive owner is the existing Engine F1 epic; exact clause membership remains query-derived.

rows.requirement: Select a seeded table, pool, percentage, or shared roll replacement deterministically
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness clauses whose hook engine is qualified as engine:F2 and whose hook name contains activation or action-economy; derive membership from the committed records, not a stored total.
rows.codeEvidence: Seeded dice, table, pool, and replacement selection are available through the deterministic roll surface; source-specific selection ownership is not yet clause-complete.
rows.notes: This is F1's selection primitive even when an old engine epic used a dice-grammar label; do not infer ownership from matching numbers.

rows.requirement: Own one combatant's action, bonus-action, reaction, movement note, and free object interaction for the turn window
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F2 with action-economy or activation semantics; the query groups clauses by hook text, not family totals.
rows.codeEvidence: packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts provides durable turn-budget state, turn reset, surprise guards, and reaction allowances; item and feature callers still need clause-level wiring.
rows.notes: Existing F2 family epic owns the shared budget; this does not claim a full action-legality engine.

rows.requirement: Spend and validate reaction, item-activation, and controlled-entity command budgets at their canonical owner
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F2 whose hook is reaction, controlled-entity command, or item activation; no hand-copied hook count is retained.
rows.codeEvidence: Turn-budget and usage primitives exist, but magic-item and owned-entity activation callers are not uniformly wired to one canonical spend owner.
rows.notes: The old eshyra-2n1t.4 bead is historical context only; the qualified pack family is owned by the open F2 epic.

rows.requirement: Track a legendary creature's per-round allowance, per-option cost, spend window, and start-of-turn recovery
rows.packEvidence: Negative pack query: emit record.key for every data.executionReadiness clause with a qualified engine:F2 hook, then compare it with the source/audit legendary-action inventory; the missing budget clause is not discoverable from projected mechanics alone.
rows.codeEvidence: actionEconomy.ts and usageCounters.ts contain allowance, cost, and per-round reset primitives, but the source-defined legendary budget and every option are not projected into the pack execution path.
rows.notes: Worked non-pack-discovery example: the source clause and audit expose the budget even where the projected mechanics do not.

rows.requirement: Maintain one concentration effect per owner and resolve the damage-triggered concentration save with a source-grounded DC
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F3 whose hook contains concentration; group by hook text and clause key.
rows.codeEvidence: activeEffects.ts and the HP mutation seams implement concentration ownership, damage-save evidence, incapacitation breaks, and terminal cleanup; remaining work is clause-wide integration.
rows.notes: The old eshyra-2n1t.5 acceptance covered this foundation, not every F3 hook in the later clause-complete pack.

rows.requirement: Create, expire, suppress, refresh, and terminate duration-bearing active effects at the canonical lifecycle seam
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F3 with duration, active-effect, or lifecycle text; membership is derived from clause keys.
rows.codeEvidence: The active-effect state machine owns typed timers, suppression, refresh, target cleanup, and terminal transitions; summoned and item-created entities still need complete source-clause wiring.
rows.notes: Duration state is a specific primitive, not a family-level claim.

rows.requirement: Own summoned or created entities and their repeat-save, repeat-damage, cleanup, and termination triggers
rows.packEvidence: Negative-plus-source query: compare records[] data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F3 with the audit's source clauses for repeat triggers and entity ownership, emitting record.key for the projected side; omitted source clauses prove pack-only discovery is insufficient.
rows.codeEvidence: Entity links and active-effect cleanup exist, but repeat-on-damage/repeat-save and all created-entity ownership clauses are not one complete execution contract.
rows.notes: The audit's missing repeat and entity clauses are evidence of incomplete integration, not evidence that the F3 bead's narrower acceptance was false.

rows.requirement: Resolve a spell with one caster of record, source-grounded ability/DC/attack context, and an explicit effect application path
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F4 with canonical spell, caster, or spell-effect text; the query retains each clause key.
rows.codeEvidence: Spellcasting derivation, upcast, and slot primitives exist, but item casts, stored spells, and every source spell procedure do not yet share a complete canonical execution seam.
rows.notes: The owner is the qualified F4 epic, not historical eshyra-2n1t.6.

rows.requirement: Validate the spell slot level and apply deterministic upcast scaling before spell resolution
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F4 with slot, casting, or stored-spell semantics; clauses remain the membership unit.
rows.codeEvidence: spellSlots.ts and spellUpcast.ts implement single-class slot state and upcast contracts; complete pack wiring and caster ownership remain open.
rows.notes: The old F4 bead supplied a slot primitive; it did not close the pack's entire canonical-spell family.

rows.requirement: Resolve wizard spellbook copying as a spell eligibility, time, and currency/asset mutation procedure
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F4 with wizard spellbook copying semantics; compare with the source clause's economy and asset requirements rather than relying on a family row.
rows.codeEvidence: Spellbook and currency primitives exist separately, but no single provider-neutral procedure owns the complete copying cost, time, eligibility, and retained asset mutation.
rows.notes: Proposed title and parent: no existing open family bead owns this cross-family spellbook-copy procedure as one primitive. Bead created 2026-07-25 from this ledger row (was proposed-new-bead); it is blocked by its family decomposition task.

rows.requirement: Spend item-instance uses or charges against the owning instance with a durable remaining-use state
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F5 with per-item storage, charge, or usage semantics; never store the result as a copied count.
rows.codeEvidence: usageCounters.ts and item-state/custody paths provide per-owner counters and spend validation, while the pack still contains engine-pending item clauses.
rows.notes: Specific instance spend is separate from reset scheduling, attunement, and curse state.

rows.requirement: Apply turn-start recharge, dawn, short-rest, long-rest, and elapsed-time reset events to the correct counter
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F5 with recharge, dawn reset, periodic reset, or cooldown semantics; group only by the hook text.
rows.codeEvidence: Usage reset events and recharge rolls exist, but all source-defined reset timing and item-instance integrations are not yet certified together.
rows.notes: Reset scheduling is not interchangeable with F7's rest orchestration.

rows.requirement: Enforce attunement slots, duplicate/identity constraints, ending conditions, and curse persistence on an item instance
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F5 whose hook contains attunement, curse, or item-instance state; retain clause keys for ownership review.
rows.codeEvidence: attunement.ts, custody, compatibility, and curse-adjacent state paths implement substantial lifecycle checks, but not every source clause is wired to the same instance owner.
rows.notes: The old eshyra-2n1t.7 acceptance is evidence for primitives, not for clause-complete integration.

rows.requirement: Persist per-instance containment/portal ownership and licensed random/card-pool state across item operations
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for projected data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F5 with containment, portal, or card-pool text, then compare against source inventory clauses named by the audit.
rows.codeEvidence: Item custody and persistent state primitives exist, but the complete containment/portal/card-pool execution contract has no exact existing owner in the current family decomposition.
rows.notes: Proposed title and parent: this is a cross-item state primitive not named as a complete deliverable by an existing open bead. Bead created 2026-07-25 from this ledger row (was proposed-new-bead); it is blocked by its family decomposition task.

rows.requirement: Apply damage, healing, maximum HP, temporary HP consumption, and dead/healing restrictions at the HP seam
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F6 with hit-point, healing, or temporary-hit-point semantics; source clauses remain query membership.
rows.codeEvidence: hpLifecycle.ts implements HP writes, healing restrictions, temporary HP ownership, and durable life state; complete source-clause integration remains open.
rows.notes: The primitive is narrower than the F6 family label and includes no hand-copied readiness total.

rows.requirement: Resolve death-save results, instant-death overflow, stable recovery, and dying/dead transitions durably
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F6 with death, dying, death-save, or stabilization semantics.
rows.codeEvidence: The death-save and life-state machine exists on the HP write path; follow-up recovery and source-specific clauses still need the clause-complete engine contract.
rows.notes: The old eshyra-2n1t.8 close reason proves its stated state machine landed, not that all F6 source clauses are integrated.

rows.requirement: Advance suffocation and recurring damage state to the correct HP/life/condition transition with fail-closed timing
rows.packEvidence: Negative-plus-source query: emit record.key for projected data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F6, then compare to audit-named suffocation and ongoing-damage clauses that are absent or only partially projected.
rows.codeEvidence: HP and condition mutation seams exist, but a complete source-grounded suffocation countdown and recurring-damage lifecycle is not certified in the current core.
rows.notes: Missing-source clauses explain the non-pack discovery; they do not make the prior F6 bead's narrower close objectively false.

rows.requirement: Spend a durable hit-dice pool during a bounded short rest and restore HP from the source-defined die procedure
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F7 with short-rest, hit-dice, or recovery semantics.
rows.codeEvidence: rest.ts and the hit-dice ledger implement durable short-rest recovery; the complete dependency and source-clause inventory remains under the F7 epic.
rows.notes: Short-rest recovery is a primitive, not a synonym for the whole rest engine.

rows.requirement: Enforce long-rest duration/eligibility gates and orchestrate F4, F5, F6, and active-effect reset hooks
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F7 with long-rest, reset, or early-reuse semantics; retain one row per hook primitive.
rows.codeEvidence: Rest orchestration and reset hooks exist with durable world time and rollback tests, but pack clauses still require complete integration and ownership proof.
rows.notes: The old eshyra-2n1t.9 close evidence establishes the rest foundation; it does not erase current engine-pending item hooks.

rows.requirement: Persist elapsed-time clocks for planar return, declared draws, timed curses, and other source-defined deadlines
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F7 with planar-return, declared-window, duration, or deadline semantics; compare with source clauses named by the audit.
rows.codeEvidence: Elapsed world timers and expiry sweeps exist, but the source-specific planar-return and declared-window procedures have no exact existing owner as one tested primitive.
rows.notes: Proposed title and parent: existing F7 owns generic rest/time orchestration but not this cross-record source-clock contract. Bead created 2026-07-25 from this ledger row (was proposed-new-bead); it is blocked by its family decomposition task.

rows.requirement: Derive save DC and spell attack modifiers from the qualified ability, proficiency, and item effects
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F8 with save DC, spell attack, or derived combat modifier text.
rows.codeEvidence: Derived values, spellcasting derivation, and resolution tools implement the basic modifier paths; special source qualifiers and item bonuses remain clause work.
rows.notes: The old F8 character-build bead is not the owner; the qualified pack F8 epic is.

rows.requirement: Represent multiple saves, alternative save abilities, repeat saves, and save-dependent outcomes without dropping later branches
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F8 with save, ability-choice, or targeting consequences; compare each clause key with the audit's multi-save inventory.
rows.codeEvidence: Checks and saves have typed resolution primitives, but the audit's multi-save and ability-choice branches are not uniformly represented in the source projection.
rows.notes: A DC field alone is not evidence that the complete structured save outcome exists.

rows.requirement: Apply source-qualified attack, AC, proficiency, advantage, and disadvantage modifiers exactly once
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F8 with attack, damage, roll mode, or derived combat modifier text.
rows.codeEvidence: Derived-value and D20 resolution primitives exist, but item, class, and conditional modifier ownership is not yet clause-complete.
rows.notes: This row separates modifier application from the save/DC row and keeps source qualifiers visible.

rows.requirement: Resolve point-origin areas, range, cover, targets, and forced-movement geometry with source-defined variants
rows.packEvidence: Negative-plus-source query: emit record.key for projected data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F9 with geometry or targeting text, then compare to audit-named point-origin clauses absent from projection.
rows.codeEvidence: Deterministic checks and movement arithmetic exist, but the core has no complete point-origin geometry and source-variant targeting contract.
rows.notes: Point-origin geometry is a source-clause gap even though the existing F9 epic is the appropriate broad engine owner.

rows.requirement: Resolve typed damage riders, resistance/vulnerability, ongoing damage, and half-damage-on-success alternatives
rows.packEvidence: Negative-plus-source query: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F9 with damage or rider text, then compare with audit-named half-damage and rider clauses not projected.
rows.codeEvidence: resolve_damage provides typed packet and resistance/vulnerability math, but source-defined riders, recurring branches, and every half-damage alternative are not integrated.
rows.notes: The audit's creature and hazard half-damage branches are source evidence, not a copied ledger count.

rows.requirement: Resolve deterministic contests, escapes, forced movement, destruction, and object interaction outcomes
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F9 with movement, contest, escape, destruction, or interaction text.
rows.codeEvidence: resolve_contest, calc, and damage primitives exist, but object and source-specific movement procedures still require canonical wiring.
rows.notes: The row names the actual resolution primitive rather than repeating the F9 family label.

rows.requirement: Compute carrying, vehicle pull, coverage, time, volume, and source-defined variant quantities deterministically
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F9 with capacity, coverage, time, volume, or size-scaled quantity text.
rows.codeEvidence: The calc primitive covers several SRD formulas, but complete source-variant semantics and object/property callers are not certified.
rows.notes: Arithmetic formula presence is not proof of every surrounding execution branch.

rows.requirement: Read, earn, spend, convert, and audit currency mutations through the canonical gameplay surface
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F10 with currency, property, inventory, or XP ledger semantics.
rows.codeEvidence: character/currency.ts and CLI money commands implement denomination conversion, but the DM-facing canonical mutation/context surface is not complete.
rows.notes: The old eshyra-2n1t.12 close reason is evidence for the currency surface slice, not all F10 asset procedures.

rows.requirement: Apply deterministic downtime study, lifestyle expense, profession, research, and training ledger transformations
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F10 with downtime, study, expense, profession, research, or training text.
rows.codeEvidence: Currency primitives can support these calculations, but no complete canonical DM tool owns their source-defined time and ledger outcomes.
rows.notes: Trade pacing remains a DM ruling; this row covers only deterministic ledger mutations named by source clauses.

rows.requirement: Create and retain canonical inventory, property, XP, and other source-defined assets with auditable ownership
rows.packEvidence: Generated query over records[]: emit record.key for data.executionReadiness hooks qualified as engine:F10 with retained asset creation, inventory, property, or XP semantics; source omissions are compared separately.
rows.codeEvidence: Character progression and inventory structures exist, but there is no exact existing owner for the full retained-asset creation and provenance contract.
rows.notes: Proposed title and parent: current F10 owns currency/downtime surface, but retained asset creation and provenance cross its existing boundary. Bead created 2026-07-25 from this ledger row (was proposed-new-bead); it is blocked by its family decomposition task.
